title: Terms on Which the Premium Difference of a Repriced Protection Plan Falls Due
content:
When the premium of a Pass and Trip Protection plan has been worked out afresh, the difference between it and
the premium frozen on the plan falls due in one of three ways.

**Where an entry for a move up of tier stands on the covered holding's Season Pass Programme account for the
season and the plan's premium is collected alongside that holding's instalments**, the difference is spread
over the days of cover still to come, counted from the day the change takes effect to the day cover is due to
end, as a share of the days from the day cover began to the day cover is due to end.

**Where no entry for a move up of tier stands on the covered holding's account for the season and the plan's
premium is collected alongside that holding's instalments**, the difference is spread evenly over the
instalments still to fall on the covered holding's schedule, as a share of all the instalments that schedule
holds.

**In every other case** the whole difference falls due at once.

**Worked examples (hypothetical inputs).** Take a plan collected alongside the covered holding's instalments,
cover running 150 days from the day it began to the day it is due to end, an entry for a move up of tier
standing on that holding's account for the season, and the change taking effect with 60 of those days still to
come. The share is 60 days over 150 days, which is two fifths, so two fifths of the difference falls due. Take
the same plan with no such entry standing on the holding's account, the holding's schedule holding 5
instalments of which 2 still fall: the share is 2 instalments over 5 instalments, which is two fifths again,
and two fifths of the difference falls due. Take a plan whose premium is collected in a single payment: the
whole difference falls due at once, whatever the covered holding's account carries.
